correctness.rationale: The complete-graph migration operator is zero on constants and −3D on the nonuniform subspace, and acts identically on both variables. Using βs*=γ, the homogeneous quadratic is λ²+cλ+B+Z and is strictly Hurwitz. The nonuniform directed factors are λ²+hλ+k+Zκ for κ=−1/2±i√3/2. An imaginary root requires ω=∓√3Z/(2h) and k=Z/2+3Z²/(4h²); the latter is strictly increasing in Z≥0 and gives exactly the stated positive threshold. At the crossing the derivative of the root has strictly positive real part, (h/2+3Z/(2h))/(h²+3Z²/h²); its partner in the same quadratic has real part −h. Continuity from the strictly Hurwitz case Z=0 and absence of other axis roots prove the full unstable-pair count; nonreal constants preclude real roots in the spatial factors at Z>0. The reciprocal spatial factors are repeated copies of λ²+hλ+k−Z/2, so two spatial roots reach zero at 2k, strictly above the directed threshold. The function k−Z/2−3Z²/(4h²) increases strictly with D and decreases with Z, and h/D→6, k/D²→9 give the stated coefficient 12. At D=0 the one- and two-patch stochastic information eigenvalues are real; in two patches the only repeated-eigenvalue case is the identity. Each scalar factor then has imaginary part cω at λ=iω, ruling out a nonzero-frequency crossing. Endemic balance and the derivative of the frozen sigmoid give the stated witness; more generally a logistic response with intercept matched to p(i*) can realize any positive derivative at fixed equilibrium value. For a C¹ vector field the Hurwitz test here decides local exponential stability, including its failure at a purely imaginary eigenvalue, not nonlinear orbital stability.
